Rashi on Chullin 15b:10:1.english: Rabbi disqualifies [it] - We derive this below from [the verse], "and he took the knife" [referring to Abraham at the Binding of Isaac].

Rashi on Chullin 15b:10:2.hebrew: ורבי חייא מכשיר - ומתניתין דקתני שחיטתו כשרה, לא מתוקמא כרבי אלא כרבי חייא, ולכתחלה מיהת לא שחטינן, ואשמועינן מתני' דעד כאן כו':
Rashi on Chullin 15b:10:2.english: And Rabbi Chiya deems it valid - And the mishna that teaches "its slaughter is valid" cannot be reconciled with [the view of] Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], but only with [the view of] Rabbi Chiya; yet even so, ab initio we do not slaughter [in this way]. And [the Gemara] teaches us this from [the mishna's wording] "until here, etc."

Rashi on Chullin 15b:11:1.english: Whether the knife is above - As with any other act of slaughtering.

Rashi on Chullin 15b:11:2.english: And whether the knife was below and the animal's neck was above - We are not concerned that the neck might press down heavily upon the knife and sever it in one stroke, before he moves [the knife] back and forth.

Rashi on Chullin 15b:12:1.hebrew: לעולם רבי חייא ואפילו לכתחלה - נמי מכשר:
Rashi on Chullin 15b:12:1.english: Actually, [it follows] Rabbi Ḥiyya's view, and even ab initio - he also deems it valid.

Rashi on Chullin 15b:15:1.english: There is a contradiction between [the rulings of] Rabbi and [those of] Rabbi - For it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi renders it unfit, which implies [that it is unfit] even after the fact.

Rashi on Chullin 15b:15:2.english: Attached from the outset - [Using such a knife] invalidates [the slaughter], even after the fact.

Rashi on Chullin 15b:16:1.english: With a wheel - A wheel called a "tur," and he laid the knife in it with its edge facing up, and he turned it and slaughtered.

Rashi on Chullin 15b:16:2.english: He embedded a knife in the wall - and moved the animal's neck back and forth over it.

Rashi on Chullin 15b:16:3.hebrew: צור יוצא מן הכותל - היינו מחובר מעיקרו, דמוקמינן ליה לקמן בכותל מערה, שלא נבנה הכותל על ידי אדם, אלא חוקק בקרקע והכותל עומד מאליו, ורישא בתלוש ולבסוף חברו. והאי דהדר תנא נעץ סכין בכותל, איצטריך לאשמועינן דאף על גב דלא מבטל ליה, אפילו הכי לכתחלה לא ישחוט. קנה עומד מאליו - שלא נטעו אדם שם, אלא מעצמו עלה:
Rashi on Chullin 15b:16:3.english:
A rock protruding from the wall - This is [a case of] "attached from the outset," for we establish it below [in the Gemara] as referring to the wall of a cave, where the wall was not built by a person, but rather [the cave] was hollowed out of the ground and the wall stands on its own. And the first clause [of the mishna] refers to [a case of] "detached and then attached." And the reason [the mishna] then taught [the case of] "one stuck a knife into the wall" was necessary, to teach us that even though he does not nullify it [as a utensil], nevertheless one should not slaughter with it ab initio.
"A reed that stands on its own" - Meaning, that no person planted it there, but rather it grew up by itself.

Rashi on Chullin 15b:1:1.hebrew: שהיה לו חולה - מע"ש, דכיון דשוגג הוא כדאוקמינן, וליכא איסור שבת, איסור מוקצה נמי ליכא, דעומדת לשחיטה היתה בין השמשות, ואפילו בשבת משום דחולי דפיקוח נפש דוחה את השבת:
Rashi on Chullin 15b:1:1.english: That he had a sick person - [This means] from before Shabbat, since it is a case of unwitting error, as we established, and thus there is no violation of Shabbat; nor is there a violation of muktzeh either, since it [the animal] was designated for slaughter at twilight [before Shabbat began]; and even [if he had it] on Shabbat itself [there would be no violation], because illness involving danger to life overrides Shabbat.

Rashi on Chullin 15b:2:1.hebrew: מ"ט דרבי יהודה - הא אפי' במזיד איסור שבת ליכא, וכ"ש בשוגג:
Rashi on Chullin 15b:2:1.english: What is Rabbi Yehuda's reason - [The Gemara's question is difficult] since even if he slaughtered it intentionally [after the sick person recovered], there is no violation of the Shabbat prohibition, and all the more so if he did so unwittingly.

Rashi on Chullin 15b:2:2.hebrew: והבריא - היום בשבת איסור מוקצה ליכא, דהא בין השמשות חולה היה, הלכך לר"מ דלאו משוי שוגג דאיסור שבת שרי, ולרבי יהודה אסור, דאיסור שבת דשוגג איכא, דהא הבריא:
Rashi on Chullin 15b:2:2.english: And he recovered - Today, on Shabbat, there is no prohibition of muktze, since at twilight [when Shabbat began] he was still sick. Therefore, according to Rabbi Meir, who does not consider this to constitute an unwitting violation of a Shabbat prohibition, it is permitted; but according to Rabbi Yehuda it is forbidden, since there is an unwitting violation of a Shabbat prohibition, as he had [meanwhile] recovered.

Rashi on Chullin 15b:3:1.hebrew: וכי הא - כלומר הא דאוקימנא דמשום איסור מוקצה שתקיה רב לתנא, ואע"ג דבאיסור שבת שוגג הוה, היינו כי הא דאמר רב:
Rashi on Chullin 15b:3:1.english: And this is like that - Meaning, that which we established, that it was because of the prohibition of muktzeh that Rav remained silent to the tanna; and even though [in that case] it was an unwitting violation of Shabbat, this is like that which Rav said.

Rashi on Chullin 15b:3:2.english: One who slaughters for a sick person - Who fell ill on the day of Shabbat.

Rashi on Chullin 15b:3:3.hebrew: אסור - לאכול בריא מאותה בהמה בו ביום, דאע"ג דאיסור שבת ליכא, דפיקוח נפש דוחה את השבת, איסור מוקצה מיהא איכא, דבין השמשות מוקצה הואי, ולא היתה ראויה לישחט בשבת, דהא עדיין לא היה חולה:
Rashi on Chullin 15b:3:3.english: It is forbidden - for a healthy person to eat from that animal on that same day. For even though there is no violation of the Shabbat prohibition, since the saving of a life overrides the Shabbat, there is nevertheless the prohibition of muktzeh - since at twilight [before Shabbat began] it was muktzeh, and it was not fit to be slaughtered on Shabbat, since at that time there was not yet a sick person [requiring it].

Rashi on Chullin 15b:3:4.hebrew: המבשל - בשר שהיתה שחוטה מאתמול ובשלה היום לחולה שנחלה היום, מותר לבריא:
Rashi on Chullin 15b:3:4.english: One who cooks - Meat that was slaughtered the day before, and he cooked it today for a sick person who fell ill today, is permitted for a healthy person [to eat as well].

Rashi on Chullin 15b:4:1.hebrew: מ"ט האי - בשר הוה חזי להאי בריא בין השמשות לכוס חי, הילכך אין כאן איסור מוקצה, ואיסור שבת נמי אין כאן, דהא לחולה בשלה:
Rashi on Chullin 15b:4:1.english: What is the reason for this - The meat was fit for this healthy person to chew raw at twilight; therefore, there is no prohibition of muktzeh here, and there is also no prohibition of Shabbat here, since he cooked it for the sick person.

Rashi on Chullin 15b:4:2.hebrew: והאי - שוחט לא היה בין השמשות ראוי לכוס, ואיכא איסור מוקצה, אע"ג דאיסור שבת ליכא:
Rashi on Chullin 15b:4:2.english: And this one - The animal to be slaughtered was not, at twilight, fit to be eaten, and therefore it is subject to the prohibition of muktzeh [being set aside from use], even though there is no violation of the Shabbat prohibition [since slaughtering for a sick person is permitted].

Rashi on Chullin 15b:5:1.english: Sometimes the slaughterer - [When it says that the slaughtering] for the sick person is permitted, it is [also] permitted for a healthy person to eat [from it as well] - for example, if he already had a sick person [in mind] from before [the onset of] the day, in which case there is neither a violation of muktzeh nor a violation of Shabbat here.

Rashi on Chullin 15b:5:2.english: And one who cooks - [This is referring to cooking] for a person who fell sick today; [the food] is forbidden to a healthy person.

Rashi on Chullin 15b:5:3.hebrew: כגון שקצץ דלעת - מן המחובר, ובשלה לו, דיש כאן איסור מוקצה, דמחוברת היתה בין השמשות. ואית דמפרשי בדלעת תלושה, ומוקצה דידה משום דקשה היא, ולא היא, חדא דדלעת רכה היא יותר מן הבשר, ועוד קצץ מן המחובר משמע דאי בתלושה לא שייך קציצה אלא חיתוך, כגון (שבת דף קנו:) מחתכין את הדילועין לפני הבהמה:
Rashi on Chullin 15b:5:3.english: For example, he cut off a gourd - From that which was attached [to the ground], and he cooked it for him, for there is here a prohibition of muktzeh, since it was attached [to the ground] at twilight. And there are those who explain this regarding a gourd that was already detached, and its muktzeh status is because it is hard. But that is not so: first, because a gourd is softer than meat; and furthermore, "he cut off" implies from that which is attached, for if it were detached, the term "cutting off" would not apply, but rather "cutting," as, for example, (Shabbat 156b): "They cut gourds before an animal."

Rashi on Chullin 15b:6:1.english: The halakha is: one who slaughters for an ill person on Shabbat - [This refers to a case] where the ill person [was already ill] while it was still day, [before Shabbat].

Rashi on Chullin 15b:6:3.hebrew: אדעתא דחולה קא שחיט - וליכא למגזר שמא ירבה בשחיטה בשביל בריא, דהא משום ההוא זית דחולה בעי למשחט כולה:
Rashi on Chullin 15b:6:3.english: He is slaughtering with the sick person in mind - And there is no need to be concerned that he will slaughter excessively for the healthy person, since on account of that single olive's-worth [needed] for the sick person, he must slaughter the entire animal [anyway].

Rashi on Chullin 15b:7:1.hebrew: במגל יד - רפש"א בלע"ז, ויש לה שתי פיות: האחת חלקה כסכין, והאחת יש בה פגימות:
Rashi on Chullin 15b:7:1.english: With a hand sickle - "Rapsa" in Old French. It has two edges: one smooth like a knife, and the other notched [like a saw].

Rashi on Chullin 15b:8:1.hebrew: הכל שוחטין ובכל שוחטין - כולה מפרש בגמרא:
Rashi on Chullin 15b:8:1.english: All may slaughter, and with anything one may slaughter - [The Gemara] explains all of this.

Rashi on Chullin 15b:8:2.hebrew: מגל קציר - שקוצרין בה התבואה, פלציל"א בלע"ז, שפגימותיה נוטות כולן לצד אחד בשיפוע:
Rashi on Chullin 15b:8:2.english: A harvest sickle - With which they harvest the grain; "faucille" in the vernacular, whose notches all slant in one direction, at a slope.

Rashi on Chullin 15b:8:3.hebrew: מגירה - סכין מלא פגימות, ואין משופעות כשל מגל קציר, אלא מכוונות, שיש לפגימה מורשא מכאן ומכאן, כסתם פגימות אוגרת. ומגירה בלעז סייג"א:
Rashi on Chullin 15b:8:3.english: A saw [megeirah] - A knife full of notches, which are not slanted like those of a harvest sickle, but rather straight, such that each notch has a ridge on this side and on that side, like the ordinary notches a knife accumulates [through use]. And "megeirah" in the vernacular is "scie" [saw].

Rashi on Chullin 15b:8:4.english: Teeth - That are set in the jaw of the animal.

Rashi on Chullin 15b:8:5.english: And the fingernail - [Meaning] while still attached [to the finger].

Rashi on Chullin 15b:8:6.hebrew: שהם חונקין - שאין חותכין אלא קורעין מחמת הפגימות. והאי חונקין אשארא קאי, ולאו אצפורן, דטעמא דצפורן מפרש בגמרא משום מחובר:
Rashi on Chullin 15b:8:6.english: That they strangle - [Meaning] that they do not cut but rather tear, because of the nicks [in their edge]. And this [reason of] "they strangle" refers to the rest [of the disqualified implements], but not to the fingernail; for the reason for [the disqualification of] the fingernail is explained in the Gemara as being because it is attached [to the body].

Rashi on Chullin 15b:9:1.hebrew: דלמא אתי למעבד באידך גיסא - במקום הפגימות. ושמעינן מהא דסכין פגומה ויש בה כדי לשחוט מן הפגם ולהלן, אסור לשחוט בה לכתחלה, דהא הכא גזרינן משום אידך גיסא, וכל שכן הכא דבההיא גיסא גופה פגומה:
Rashi on Chullin 15b:9:1.english: Lest he come to perform [the slaughter] with the other side - [Meaning,] at the place of the notches. And we learn from this that a knife which is nicked, but has enough [smooth blade] to slaughter from the nick onward, is forbidden to slaughter with ab initio, since here too we decree on account of [using] the other side - and all the more so here [in the case of the sickle], where that other side is itself [entirely] notched.

Rashi on Chullin 15b:9:2.english: Krumit - The rib [i.e., ridge] of a reed.

Tosafot on Chullin 15b:12:1.hebrew: להודיעך כחו דרבי - ולא חייש לאשמועי' כח דהיתרא דרבי חייא, דכבר אשמועינן בברייתא דבכל שוחטין, בין בתלוש בין במחובר:
Tosafot on Chullin 15b:12:1.english: To inform you of the strength of Rabbi's [opinion] - And [the Gemara] is not concerned to teach [us] the strength of the leniency of Rabbi Chiya, because it already taught us in the Baraita that one may slaughter with anything, whether it is detached or attached.

Tosafot on Chullin 15b:15:1.hebrew: כאן במחובר מעיקרו - לעיל גבי רבי חייא לא הוה מצי לשנויי הכי, דכיון דמחובר מעיקרו כשר בדיעבד, למה יאסור לכתחלה? דאי משום שמא ידרוס, א"כ תלוש ולבסוף חיברו נמי:
Tosafot on Chullin 15b:15:1.english: Here, [we are dealing with something] attached from the outset - Above, regarding Rabbi Chiya, [the Gemara] could not have answered in this way. For since [something] attached from the outset is valid after the fact (be-di'avad), why would it be forbidden ab initio (le-chatchilah)? For if [the reason] is because of a concern that he might commit derasah (pressing the blade rather than drawing it), then the same should hold true of [something] detached and then reattached as well.

Tosafot on Chullin 15b:16:1.hebrew: או שהיה קנה עומד מאליו - לאו למעוטי נטעו אדם קאתי, דההוא נמי חשיב מחובר מעיקרו, דאפי' למאן דאמר המשתחוה לבית אסרו, המשתחוה לאילן לא אסרו, אלא תוספת דוקא. ולא נקט הכא עולה מאליו, אלא לגלות על צור היוצא מן הכותל, דאיירי בכותל מערה דומיא דקנה העומד מאליו:
Tosafot on Chullin 15b:16:1.english: Or if there was a reed standing by itself - [This] does not come to exclude [a case where] a person planted it, for that too is considered attached from the outset (mechubar me'ikaro). For even according to the one who says: one who bows down to a house - they forbade it; one who bows down to a tree - they did not forbid it, [that leniency applies] only to the [subsequent] growth (tosefet) specifically. And [the Mishnah] did not state here "growing by itself" (oleh me'elav), but rather [used "standing by itself"] in order to reveal [the law] regarding the rock protruding from the wall, since it deals with the wall of a cave, similar to the reed that stands by itself.

Tosafot on Chullin 15b:2:1.hebrew: כגון שהיה לו חולה והבריא - וא"ת: אם יש מוקצה לחצי שבת, אמאי שרי לר"מ בשוחט לחולה והבריא? ור' יהודה נמי, אמאי לא אסר משום מוקצה? דלא אסר אלא משום דקניס שוגג אטו מזיד, כדאמרינן בהניזקין (גיטין נג:), דבעיא היא בשילהי אין צדין (ביצה דף כו:) אם יש מוקצה לחצי שבת אם לאו. וי"ל, כיון שרגילות הוא שחוזר לחוליו, לא הוי מוקצה, כמו גמרו בידי אדם דשרי התם. אי נמי, רב גופיה מספקא ליה דשמא אין מוקצה לחצי שבת, ולהכי לא אוקמיה כר"מ אלא כר' יהודה דאסר משום דקניס שוגג אטו מזיד:
Tosafot on Chullin 15b:2:1.english: For example, he had a sick person and [the sick person] recovered - And if you say: if there is [a concept of] muktzeh for half of Shabbat, why is it permitted according to R. Meir in the case of one who slaughters for a sick person who then recovers? And according to R. Yehuda too, why did he not prohibit it on account of muktzeh, seeing that he prohibited it only because he penalizes [one who acted] unwittingly on account of [one who might act] deliberately, as we say in [the chapter] HaNizakin (Gittin 53b), for it is an unresolved question at the end of [the chapter] Ein Tzadin (Beitzah 26b) whether there is muktzeh for half of Shabbat or not? And one can answer: since it is usual for [the animal] to relapse into its illness, it is not considered muktzeh — just like [the case of] "its completion was performed by human hand," which is permitted there. Alternatively, Rav himself was in doubt whether perhaps there is no muktzeh for half of Shabbat, and therefore he did not establish [the ruling] like R. Meir but like R. Yehuda, who prohibits it because he penalizes [one who acted] unwittingly on account of [one who might act] deliberately.

Tosafot on Chullin 15b:5:1.hebrew: כגון שקצץ לו דלעת - פירש בקונטרס: מדנקט "קצץ" משמע דאיירי מן המחובר, וקשה, דא"כ מאי איריא מבשל, אפילו כי לא נתבשל נמי אסור. ואומר ר"ת דבתלושה איירי, ושייך נמי בתלושה לשון קציצה, כמו כאן "קיצץ בן עזאי תורמוסי תרומה" בפ' במה מדליקין (שבת דף לד.), ובריש פרק אחד דיני ממונות (סנהדרין דף לג:) "אדמוקדך יקוד, קוץ קרך וצלי", דבתלושה איירי. והא דלא נקט לשון חתיכה, כדתנן (שבת דף קנו:) "מחתכין את הדילועין", לפי שדרך לקוצצן בחתיכות גדולות כשבאין לבשל, שייך בו לשון קציצה. ומבשל אסור, משום דדלעת לא חזיא לכוס, כדאמרינן במס' תמיד (דף כז:) "כל מידי לא תפלט קמי רבך, בר מקרא חייא, דכפתילה של אבר דמיא". וא"ת: והא חזיא לבהמה, ומוכן לכלבים הוי מוכן לאדם, כדמסיק בפ"ק דביצה (דף ו:) גבי אפרוח שנולדה בי"ט. וי"ל, כיון דדלעת עומדת לאדם ואינה ראויה לאדם, הוי מוקצה, אע"ג דחזיא לבהמה:
Tosafot on Chullin 15b:5:1.english: For example, where he cut off a gourd for him - Rashi explained: since it uses the word "cut off" (kitzetz), this implies that it is discussing [a gourd] that is still attached [to the ground]. But this is difficult: if so, why does [the Gemara] specify "cooks"? Even if it were not cooked, it would also be forbidden [since it was attached on Yom Tov]. And Rabbeinu Tam says that it is discussing a detached [gourd], and the term "cutting" (kitzitzah) applies to a detached one as well, just as here: "Ben Azzai cut lupine of terumah" in the chapter "Bameh Madlikin" (Shabbat 34a), and at the beginning of the chapter "Echad Dinei Mamonot" (Sanhedrin 33b): "While your fire is kindled, cut your gourd and roast it" - these deal with a detached item. And the reason it did not use the term "cutting into pieces" (chatichah), as we learned (Shabbat 156b) "they cut gourds into pieces," is that it is customary to cut them into large pieces when one comes to cook them, [so] the term "kitzitzah" applies to it. And cooking [it] is forbidden, because a gourd is not fit to be eaten [raw], as we say in Tractate Tamid (27b): "Do not spit out anything in front of your teacher, except for the gourd of Chiya (kra chiya), for it is comparable to a wick made of lead." And if you say: but it is fit for an animal, and "designated for dogs" counts as "designated for a person," as is concluded in the first chapter of Beitzah (6b) regarding a chick hatched on Yom Tov - one can answer: since a gourd is [normally] intended for a person, and it is not fit for a person [in its raw state], it is muktzeh, even though it is fit for an animal.

Tosafot on Chullin 15b:9:1.hebrew: אלא צור וקנה לכתחלה לא - וא"ת: ודלמא נקט לשון דיעבד משום מגל יד, כדאשכחן בריש כל הפסולין (זבחים דף לב.) דנקט ששחט משום טמא, אע"ג דזרים ונשים ועבדים שוחטין לכתחלה. וי"ל דהתם ניחא ליה למינקט כל הפסולין בעבודה יחד, דשחיטה כשרה, אבל כאן מה לו לשנות יחד כשרים לכתחלה עם כשרים בדיעבד. וא"ת, דבפ' חבית (שבת קמז.) קתני הרוחץ דיעבד משום מי מערה, אע"ג דחמי טבריא אפי' לכתחלה. וי"ל דמש"ה קתני חמי טבריא בהדי מי מערה, למידק נמי דמי מערה חמין דומיא דמי טבריא, כדאמר התם:
Tosafot on Chullin 15b:9:1.english: Rather, a flint and a reed, not ab initio - And if you should say: perhaps [the Mishnah] uses the language of "after the fact" (bedieved) on account of the hand-sickle, as we find at the beginning of [the chapter] "Kol HaPesulin" (Zevachim 32a), which states "he slaughtered" [i.e., bedieved language] regarding a tamei (impure) person, even though non-priests, women, and slaves may slaughter ab initio? One can answer that there, it was fitting [for the Mishnah] to state all the disqualified persons together with regard to the service, since the slaughtering [performed by any of them] is valid; but here, why would it need to teach together, in one clause, cases valid ab initio with cases valid [only] after the fact? And if you should say: in Perek "Chavit" (Shabbat 147a) it teaches [that] one who washes [is permitted, but only] after the fact, on account of cave water, even though [washing in] the hot springs of Tiberias [is permitted] even ab initio? One can answer that this is precisely why it teaches the hot springs of Tiberias together with cave water - in order to also deduce that cave water is hot, similar to the water of Tiberias, as it says there.

Tosafot on Chullin 15b:9:2.hebrew: ורמינהי בכל שוחטין בין בצור - הוה מצי למימר: בשלמא קנה אקנה לא קשיא, הא בסימוניא דאגמא הא בשאר קנה, כמו שמחלק לקמן (חולין דף טז:), אלא צור אצור קשיא:
Tosafot on Chullin 15b:9:2.english: And we raise a contradiction: "With anything one may slaughter, whether with a flint..." - He could have said: Granted, [the contradiction between the sources regarding] reed against reed is not difficult - this [source] is referring to [reed from] Simonya of the marsh, and that [source] is referring to another kind of reed, as he distinguishes below (Chullin 16b); but [the contradiction regarding] flint against flint remains difficult.
